title: Egg omelet or scrambled egg with tomatoes, fat added

content.title: About
content.content: Egg omelet or scrambled egg with tomatoes is a dish made from eggs cooked together with diced tomatoes and a small amount of fat (oil, butter, or other cooking fat). Eggs provide a complete set of proteins, while tomatoes add vitamin C, lycopene, and fresh flavor.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Tomatoes cooked with eggs increase lycopene absorption thanks to the added fat.
Eggs contain all essential amino acids, making them a high‑quality protein source.
The dish can be prepared in under 10 minutes.
Around the world, variations include different herbs and spices, but the basic recipe stays the same.
The combination of eggs and tomatoes may boost mood due to tryptophan content.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: Eggs supply high‑quality protein essential for muscle growth and tissue repair.

items.title: Source of vitamin D and B12
items.content: Eggs are one of the few natural foods providing vitamin D and vitamin B12, important for bone health and nervous system function.

items.title: Lycopene from tomatoes
items.content: Lycopene is a powerful antioxidant that supports heart health and may reduce the risk of certain cancers.

items.title: Healthy fats
items.content: A modest amount of cooking oil adds monounsaturated and polyunsaturated fatty acids needed for overall health.

items.title: Eye health support
items.content: Lutein and zeaxanthin in the yolk help protect eyes from age‑related degeneration.

items.title: Egg allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to egg proteins.

items.title: Cholesterol content
items.content: Egg yolks contain cholesterol; people with high cholesterol should consume in moderation.

items.title: Excessive fat
items.content: Using too much oil can increase calorie count and lead to formation of unhealthy trans fats.

items.title: Salt and seasoning
items.content: Over‑salting adds strain to kidneys and the cardiovascular system.

content.title: How to Cook
content.content: Beat the eggs, stir in diced tomatoes and a pinch of salt. Heat a pan, melt a small amount of oil, pour in the egg mixture and stir gently until the desired consistency is reached. Optional additions include herbs, cheese, or spices.

content.title: Storage
content.content: The omelet is best enjoyed fresh. If needed, store in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 24 hours. Reheat in a pan or microwave before serving.
